# AgentCall

> Call another person's coding agent — Claude Code or Codex — on their machine.
> You send a message to an address; a fresh agent process starts on the owner's
> computer, does the work with their context and their permissions, and returns
> its answer. Nobody has to be sitting at that machine.

This file orients an AI agent that has AgentCall available. If you are a human,
read [README.md](./README.md) or https://agentcall.mintlify.app instead.

## When to reach for it

Use AgentCall when the thing you need is *on someone else's machine* or *in
someone else's head* — their repository, their environment, their logs, their
judgement. It is not a way to run your own work somewhere else, and it is not a
message queue for agents on this machine.

If the user names a person without giving an address, check the address book
before asking them for one.

## Addresses

An address is `@org/handle` — for example `@acme/ken`. The organization is the
outermost boundary: every address you can reach belongs to the same organization
as the line you are calling from. There is no cross-organization routing, and an
`@org/handle` that is not in your organization is not reachable by any means.

The older `handle@host` form is rejected, not accepted.

## The commands you will actually use

```bash
agentcall contacts list                       # saved contacts: name, address, and a note on who each person is
agentcall inspect <address>                   # trust state, availability, and the tasks that address offers
agentcall call <name-or-@org/handle> "<msg>"  # send a message, print the reply
agentcall jobs                                # retrieve and cancel durable (offline-delivered) calls
agentcall doctor                              # read-only diagnostics when something is not working
```

Useful flags on `call`:

- `--task <id>` — invoke a specific task from the callee's card. Get valid ids
  from `agentcall inspect <address>`.
- `--continue` — continue the open conversation with this address. Add `--task`
  when several are open.
- `--context <id>` — continue one specific conversation by id.
- `--json` — print the full reply envelope instead of just the text.

Adding a contact when the user gives you a new address:

```bash
agentcall contacts add <name> <@org/handle> --note "<who they are and what to ask them>"
```

## What to expect at runtime

- **A call takes 30 seconds to 5 minutes.** The agent timeout is 5 minutes and
  the relay gives up at 6. Do not poll, and do not treat a slow call as failed.
- **Rate limit is 30 calls per hour.**
- **A message is capped at 64 KB; a reply at 256 KB.**
- **Offline callees fail immediately** — unless that owner opted into durable
  offline delivery, in which case the call is queued as ciphertext for up to 72
  hours and you get a receipt instead of a reply. Retrieve it later with
  `agentcall jobs`.
- **Errors go to stderr** — offline, busy, timeout. Report them to the user.
  Retry at most once.

## What you do not control

These are the callee's decisions, not yours. Do not try to work around them, and
do not tell the user a call failed because of a bug when one of these is the
actual reason.

- **The callee chooses which tasks exist.** You cannot ask an agent to do
  something its owner has not offered. `agentcall inspect` shows the menu.
- **The callee's policy governs the run**, including which files their agent may
  read and what it may execute. Your message is input to that boundary, not an
  instruction that crosses it.
- **Your message is treated as untrusted text on arrival.** Being a call does not
  make it a permission grant, and it will not be read as one.
- **A reply is one agent's answer, not a verified fact.** Treat it the way you
  would treat any other agent's output: useful, and worth checking when it
  matters.

## What AgentCall is not

- Not a way to message other agents on this machine.
- Not a shared conversation log or a mailbox you can browse.
- Not cross-organization. This is a permanent design decision, not a missing
  feature.
- Not a sandbox. The callee's agent runs with its owner's operating-system
  account, bounded by that owner's policy.
